q: Which Jyutping initial sounds like the y in yes?
why: Jyutping j is the y sound: 有 (jau5).

q: Which initial has a puff of air, like the ts in cats?
why: c is ts with a puff, as in 草 (cou2); z is like ds, with no puff.

q: How many syllables are in 美國人 (mei5 gwok3 jan4, American)?
why: One character is one syllable: 美, 國 and 人 are three syllables.

q: Which word has the long aa, as in father?
why: aa is long: 三 is saam1; the others have the short a.

q: How do you say 唔 (m4, not)?
o: A low hum with the lips closed
why: 唔 has no vowel: m4 is a hum through closed lips.
Check the tone number at the end: nei5 has tone 5 and hou2 has tone 2.

p: 唔該 (thanks, excuse me) in Jyutping
why: 唔該 is m4 goi1: tone 4, a low hum, then tone 1.
三 has the long aa, so it is written saam1; sam1 would be another word.
有 starts with j, which sounds like the y in yes.
去 has the rounded vowel eo: heoi3.
十 ends in p: close the lips and stop, sap6.

hint: aa is long · tone 1 · type the number after the letters
why: 三 is saam1, tone 1: high and level.

p: Type the Jyutping of 我 (I, me)
why: 我 is ngo5, with tone 5; many people say o5, but the course writes ngo5.
書 has yu, the ee sound with rounded lips: syu1.

q: Which tone is low and falling, the lowest of all?
why: Tone 4 falls low: 時 (si4).

q: Which is the Jyutping of 賣 (to sell)?
why: 賣 is maai6, tone 6; maai5 is 買, to buy.
喺 is hai2; 係 (hai6) means to be.

q: Which two words are tone twins?
why: Tone twins have the same letters and a different tone: si1 and si3.

q: 話 alone is waa6, but in 電話 (phone) it is said waa2. What is this called?
why: In some words the last syllable rises: that is a changed tone.

p: 我想買 (I want to buy) in Jyutping
why: 買 (maai5) has tone 5; with tone 6, maai6 means to sell.

p: 詩 and then 試 (poem, to try) in Jyutping
why: Tone twins: 詩 is si1 with tone 1, 試 is si3 with tone 3.
Changed tone: the second 媽 rises to tone 1.
買 has tone 5; maai6 is 賣, to sell.
四 is sei3; with tone 2, sei2 means to die.
喺 (at, in) is hai2; hai6 is to be.

p: Type the Jyutping of 賣 (to sell)
why: 賣 has tone 6: low and level. maai5 is 買, to buy.

p: Type the Jyutping of 係 (to be)
why: 係 (to be) is hai6, tone 6; hai2, with tone 2, is 喺 (at, in).

p: Type the Jyutping of 電話 (phone)
hint: two syllables · the second one rises
why: Changed tone: 話 alone is waa6, but in 電話 it rises to waa2.

q: A server brings your dish. You say…
why: For a service, say 唔該; 多謝 is for gifts and kind words.

q: Your grandma gives you a red envelope with money in it. You say…
why: Gifts and money take 多謝.

q: Someone says 多謝 to you. You answer…
why: 唔使客氣 means you're welcome: no need to be polite.

q: It is 9 a.m. and you meet your neighbor. You say…
why: 早晨 is good morning, until about noon; 早抖 is good night.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 多謝 (thank you)?
why: 多謝 is do1 ze6: tone 1, then tone 6.
Check the tone number: 謝 is ze6, tone 6, low and level.
晨 has tone 4, low and falling: zou2 san4.

p: One milk tea, please. (start with 唔該)
why: Milk tea in a cup takes the classifier 杯: 一杯奶茶.
To ask for something, start with 唔該.
For a gift, thank with 多謝; 晒 makes it stronger.
唔使客氣 answers thanks: literally, no need to be polite. 唔使多謝 and 唔使唔該 (no need to thank me) work too.
Gifts and kind words take 多謝; 唔該 is for a service.

p: Type the Jyutping of 唔該 (thanks for a service)
hint: two syllables · 唔 is a hum · tone 4, then tone 1
why: 唔該 is m4 goi1: tone 4, then tone 1.

p: One coffee, please. (start with 唔該)
why: Coffee in a cup takes the classifier 杯, between 一 and 咖啡.
The sun and the moon together make 明, bright.

q: What does 口 on the left of 嘅, 咗 and 啲 often tell you?
o: It is an everyday spoken-Cantonese word
why: Many characters for spoken-Cantonese words carry 口 on the left.

q: A sign over a door says 出口. It means…
why: 出口 is exit: 出 is out, and 口 here is an opening.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 水 (water)?
why: 水 is seoi2, tone 2: it rises from the middle.

q: Which part is a squeezed 人 (person)?
why: 亻 is the person radical, as in 休 and 你.
The describer goes before the noun: 好人, a good person.

p: 好人 (a good person) in Jyutping
why: 好 is hou2, tone 2; 人 is jan4, tone 4.

p: a big mountain (in characters; 大 = big)
why: The describer goes before the noun: 大山, a big mountain.
A person leaning on a tree makes 休, to rest.
Two trees make 林, woods.
A woman and a child make 好, good.

hint: tone 2 · it rises from the middle
why: 好 (good) has tone 2: hou2.
The describer goes before the noun: 好人.
人 has tone 4, low and falling: jan4.
係 joins two nouns, and Cantonese has no word for a here.
佢 covers he, she and it; context tells you which.
Adjectives take 好, not 係: 佢好攰。
係 is hai6; 喺 (hai2) means at, in.
哋 makes a pronoun plural: 佢哋 is they.

p: He is my friend. (start with 佢)
why: The owner goes before the noun: 我朋友, my friend.
都 goes before the verb, not at the end like English too.
唔 goes right before 係: 唔係 means are not.
係 (hai6) joins two nouns; 喺 (hai2) means at.
唔係 means is not: 唔 comes right before 係.
Adjectives take 好, not 係: 佢好攰。
The owner goes before the noun: 我朋友, my friend.

p: I am a student too. (都 = also)
why: 都 goes before the verb: 我都係學生.
係 joins two nouns: 佢哋係老師, with no word for a.
The question word stays where the answer goes: 你叫咩名呀？
叫 means to be called; 我名係 is a word-for-word copy of English.
住喺 + place: 我住喺紐約。

q: Which is the Jyutping of 叫 (to be called)?
why: 叫 is giu3, tone 3: middle and level.

q: Someone asks 你貴姓呀？ They want to know…
why: 貴姓 is the polite way to ask a family name.

p: She is my Cantonese teacher. (start with 佢)
why: The describers go before the noun: 我廣東話老師, my Cantonese teacher.
都 goes before the verb: 我都係美國人.
The question word 咩 stays where the answer goes.
叫 means to be called: 我叫 + your name.
Use 姓 for your family name: 我姓陳.
住喺 + place: 喺 (hai2) means at, in; 係 (hai6) is to be.
The describers go before the noun: 我廣東話老師, my Cantonese teacher.

p: We are from Hong Kong too. (都 = also)
why: 都 goes before the verb: 我哋都係香港人.
The question word 咩 stays where the answer goes: 你叫咩名呀？
Verb, 唔, verb: 去唔去.

q: Someone asks 你食唔食呀？ (食 = eat) To say yes, you answer…
why: Cantonese has no single word for yes: repeat the verb, 食.
唔 goes right before the adjective: 我唔攰.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 唔 (not)?
why: 唔 is m4, tone 4: low and falling.

q: 你係咪學生呀？ means the same as…
why: 係咪 is the short form of 係唔係.

p: I am not going either. (都 = also)
why: 都 goes before the verb, and 唔 comes right before 去.

p: Is she your teacher? (start with 佢)
why: The owner goes before the noun: 你老師, your teacher.
Say the adjective, then 唔, then the adjective again: 貴唔貴.
Verb + 唔 + verb makes a yes/no question: 去唔去.

p: Are you a student? Yes, I'm a student.
why: To a 係 question, answer 係 (yes) or 唔係 (no).
唔 goes right before the verb: 佢唔食.

p: I am not a student either. (都 = also)
why: 都 goes before the verb: 我都唔係學生.
The owner goes before the noun: 你朋友, your friend.
Say the verb, then 唔, then the verb again: 去唔去.
The question word stays where the answer goes.
邊個 goes where the person would go: 佢係邊個呀？
點解 is why; 點 alone is how.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 幾時 (when)?
why: 幾時 is gei2 si4: 時 has tone 4, low and falling.
幾時 is a time word, so it comes before 去.

p: Where are you going tomorrow? (start with 你; 聽日 = tomorrow)
why: Time goes before the verb: 你聽日去邊度呀？

p: When are you going to Hong Kong? (start with 你)
why: 幾時 is a time word, so it goes before the verb.
The question word stays where the answer goes: 佢係邊個呀？
咩 asks what: it sits where the food would go.
邊度 asks where: it sits where the place would go.
點解 asks why and comes first, or right after 你.

p: Where do you work? (做嘢 = to work)
why: The place goes before the verb: 你喺邊度做嘢呀？

p: When is he going to New York?
why: 幾時 is a time word, so it goes before the verb: 佢幾時去紐約呀？

p: What are you having? (食 = to eat)
why: The question word stays where the answer goes: 你食咩呀？
Before a classifier, two is 兩: 兩個人.
Cantonese counts in 萬 (10,000): 100,000 is 十萬.
一百五 is short for 一百五十; 105 is 一百零五.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 四 (four)?
why: 四 is sei3, tone 3; sei2 is 死, to die.

q: How do you read the phone number 2345, digit by digit?
why: Phone numbers are read digit by digit, and 2 there is 二.
兩, not 二, goes before a classifier: 兩個人.
二十 is twenty, and the classifier 個 goes before the noun: 二十個人.
An empty tens place takes 零: 一百零五.
兩, not 二, goes right before 個.
零 fills the empty tens place: 一百零五.
Cantonese counts in 萬 (10,000): 100,000 is 十萬.
兩, not 二, before a classifier: 兩杯奶茶.
A number needs a classifier before the noun: 十二個人.

hint: the last 十 can be dropped
why: 一百五 is short for 一百五十; 一百零五 would be 105.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 本 (the classifier for books)?
why: 本 is bun2, with tone 2, rising from the middle.
Two is 兩 before a classifier, and a drink in a cup takes 杯.
Most animals take 隻: 一隻貓.
呢 needs the book's own classifier between it and the noun: 呢本書.

q: What does 我部手機 mean?
why: Owner + classifier + noun means "my": 我部手機.
Books take the classifier 本: 三本書.
呢 + classifier + noun, and cats take the classifier 隻: 呢隻貓.
Owner + classifier + noun means my: 我部手機, with the classifier 部 for machines.
People take 個: 嗰個人.
A drink in a cup takes 杯: 一杯奶茶.
Owner + 本 + 書 means "my book".

hint: two before a classifier is 兩
why: A number needs a classifier before the noun: 兩杯咖啡, with 兩 for two.
嗰 + classifier + noun: 嗰隻貓, with the classifier 隻 for animals.
Owner + classifier + noun means my: 我本書.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 嘅?
why: 嘅 is ge3, with tone 3: mid and level.
The owner comes first, then 嘅, then the thing: 你嘅書.
嘅 at the end stands for the thing: 係我嘅 means "it's mine".

q: Which sounds most natural for 'my dad'?
why: With family, Cantonese usually drops 嘅: 我爸爸.
The owner goes first: 老師嘅手機.
The owner goes before the noun, linked by 嘅: 我朋友嘅書.
呢 + the classifier 部 before the noun, then 係我嘅 for "mine".
The owner goes before the noun: 老師嘅書.
Yours is 你嘅: the owner + 嘅 at the end.
Owner + 嘅 + thing, or owner + classifier + thing: 老師嘅手機 or 老師部手機.
With family there is usually no 嘅: 我媽媽.
The owner goes before the noun: 我朋友嘅手機.
呢 + the classifier 本 before the noun, and 係我嘅 at the end for "mine".
The owner goes before the noun: 老師嘅書, or with the classifier, 老師本書.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 媽媽 (mom)?
why: Changed tone: the second syllable of 媽媽 rises to tone 1.
細妹 is a younger sister; 家姐 is an older one.
On your father's side, grandpa is 爺爺; 公公 is your mother's father.
Age takes no 係, and the question word sits where the answer goes: 你幾多歲呀？
老公 is husband and 老婆 is wife; 公公 is a grandpa.
兩 + the classifier 個 before the noun: 兩個家姐.

p: There are five people in my family.
why: A number needs a classifier before the noun: 五個人.

p: I'm thirty this year. (start with 我)
why: Age needs no 係: 我今年三十歲.
Family members take 個: 一個細佬.
Number + 歲 gives an age, with no 係.

p: My grandma (my mom's mom) is from Hong Kong.
why: Your mother's mother is 婆婆.
兩 + the classifier 個 before the noun: 兩個細妹.

p: There are four people in my family. (start with 我屋企)
why: A number needs a classifier before the noun: 四個人.

p: I'm twenty-five this year. (start with 我)
why: Age needs no 係: 我今年二十五歲.
喺 is hai2, with tone 2; its tone twin 係 is hai6, to be.
喺 means at or in; 係 means to be, so 我係香港 says "I am Hong Kong".
喺 + place comes before the verb: 我喺屋企食飯.
The place word comes after its noun: 屋企入面.
With 住 the place comes after: 住喺邊度, and the question word sits where the answer goes.
Place with 喺 goes before the verb: 我喺銀行做嘢.

p: The book is on the table.
why: Classifier + noun is "the book", and the place word follows its noun: 枱上面.
Owner + classifier + noun is "my phone": 我部手機, with 部 for machines.
喺 (hai2), tone 2, is at or in; 係 (hai6), tone 6, is to be.

p: The bank is next to the supermarket.
why: 隔籬 is next to, and it comes after its noun: 超市隔籬.
With 住 the place comes after: 住喺九龍.
Place with 喺 goes before the verb: 我喺銀行做嘢.
Place with 喺 goes before the verb: 我喺屋企讀書.
喺 (hai2), tone 2, asks where something is; 係 with tone 6 means to be.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 冇 (not have)?
why: 冇 is mou5, with tone 5: low, rising a little.
冇 is the only negative of 有: never 唔有.
The place comes first, then 有 + the thing: 附近有間銀行.

q: How do you answer 你有冇細妹呀？ (Do you have a younger sister?) with 'No'?
why: Answer with the verb: 有 or 冇, not 係 or 唔係.
The question form of 有 is 有冇: 你有冇手機呀？
The place goes first, before the verb 有: 附近有間超市.
兩 + the classifier 部 before the noun: 兩部手機.

p: Is there an MTR station nearby?
why: The place goes before the verb: 附近有冇地鐵站呀？
冇 is the negative of 有: never 唔有.
The question form of 有 is 有冇.
Cars take 架 (部 is also heard): 一架車.

p: I don't have any older brothers.
why: 冇 is the only negative of 有: 我冇哥哥.
The place goes before the verb 有, and banks take the classifier 間.
兩 + the classifier 隻 before the noun: 兩隻貓.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 啦 (the particle for requests)?
why: 啦 is laa1, with tone 1: high and level.

q: Which ending makes 飲杯茶 an offer: 'Have some tea!'?
why: 吖 makes an offer or an invitation: 飲杯茶吖！

q: Someone asks how you are. How do you ask back 'And you?'
why: 呢 asks the same question back: 你呢？

q: A friend suggests dim sum. Which means 'OK, sure!'?
why: 啦 agrees to a suggestion: 好啦！

q: Which question sounds friendly rather than curt?
why: 呀 is the friendly default ending for a question.
Place with 喺 goes before the verb, even in a question: 你喺邊度做嘢呀？
杯 is the classifier for a cup: 飲杯茶吖, with 吖 for an offer.
吖 turns it into an invitation: 一齊去吖！
吖 makes an invitation.
呢 asks the same question back.
啦 goes on requests and urging: 快啲啦.

p: Where do you study? (end with 呀)
why: Place with 喺 goes before the verb, even in a question: 你喺邊度讀書呀？

p: Have a cup of milk tea! (an offer)
why: 杯 is the classifier for a cup, and 吖 makes it an offer.
呢 asks the same question back: 你呢？

q: Which is the Jyutping of 錢 (money) in the question 幾多錢呀？
why: In 幾多錢 the word for money has a changed tone: cin2.
幾多錢 stays together: 幾多錢呀？
貴 is expensive and 平 is cheap: 太貴喇！
毫 is ten cents, so 五毫 is fifty cents.
Inside a number, twenty is 二十; 兩 only goes straight before 蚊.
呢 + the classifier 件 before the noun: 呢件衫.
蚊 works like a classifier straight after the number: 一百蚊.

p: Could you make it a bit cheaper?
why: 平啲 is a bit cheaper, and 得唔得 asks if that's OK.
幾多錢 asks the price.
In speech, dollars are 蚊: 三十五蚊.
Two straight before 蚊 is 兩, not 二.
呢 + the classifier 本 before the noun: 呢本書幾多錢呀？
蚊 works like a classifier, so two is 兩: 兩蚊.
貴 is expensive: 太貴喇！

q: Which is the Jyutping of 碗 (bowl)?
why: 碗 is wun2, with tone 2, rising from the middle.

q: Which classifier goes with 蝦餃 (shrimp dumplings) at dim sum?
why: Dim sum comes in a steamer basket: 一籠蝦餃.
唔該 + number + classifier + drink.

q: How do you ask for the check?
why: 埋單 is the check: 唔該埋單！
走 means leave out: 走冰 is no ice.

p: I'll have a bowl of wonton noodles.
why: Noodles in a bowl take the classifier 碗 before the noun.
兩 + the classifier 碟 before the noun: 兩碟炒飯.

p: A milk tea, no ice, please. (start with 唔該)
why: Order with 唔該, not 請: 唔該，一杯奶茶走冰.

p: A bowl of wonton noodles, please.
why: Noodles in a bowl take 碗.
埋單 is the check.

p: I'll have a basket of shrimp dumplings.
why: Dim sum in a steamer basket takes 籠.

p: An iced milk tea, please. (start with 唔該)
why: A drink in a cup takes the classifier 杯 before the noun: 一杯凍奶茶.
兩 + the classifier 籠 before the noun: 兩籠蝦餃.
唔該 is the thanks for a service: 唔該埋單！

q: Which is the Jyutping of 聽日 (tomorrow)?
why: 聽日 is ting1 jat6: tone 1, then tone 6.
而家 (now) + 幾點 (what time): 而家幾點呀？
星期 + six: 星期六. 六月 is June.
琴日 is yesterday, 聽日 tomorrow, 今日 today.
The hour first, then the minutes: 三點十分.

p: I'm going to Hong Kong tomorrow. (start with 我)
why: Time goes before the verb: 我聽日去香港.

p: We're having dim sum on Saturday. (start with 我哋)
why: The time word goes before the verb: 我哋星期六飲茶.
Month first, then day: 十二月三號.
點 is o'clock: 三點半.

p: I'm going to Hong Kong tomorrow.
why: 聽日 is tomorrow, and it goes before the verb.
號 is the day of the month: 十二月三號.

p: I'm going to Hong Kong tomorrow.
why: Time goes before the verb: 我聽日去香港.

p: I'm having dim sum on Sunday.
why: The time word goes before the verb: 我星期日飲茶.
而家 (now) comes first, then 幾點.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 瞓 (to sleep)?
why: 瞓 is fan3, tone 3: mid and level.

q: 'I eat at home in the evening' =
why: When and where both come before the verb 食飯.
食晏 is lunch: 晏晝 is the middle of the day.
A clock time goes before the verb.

q: Which question asks 'What time do you go to work?'
why: 幾點 sits where the answer would go, in front of 返工.

p: I take the MTR to work in the morning (start with 我)
why: When and how both go before the verb: 朝早 + 搭地鐵 + 返工.

p: I eat at home in the evening (start with 我)
why: Time and place go before the verb: 夜晚 + 喺屋企 + 食飯. The place word is 喺, not 係.

p: What time do you go to bed?
why: 幾點 takes the time slot, before the verb 瞓覺.
喺 (at, in) brings in the place, and the place comes before 食飯.

p: I sometimes take the MTR to work.
why: 有時 means sometimes; 每日 is every day and 成日 is often.

p: What time do you get off work?
why: 放工 is to get off work; 返工 is to go to work.

p: I take the MTR to work (use 搭)
why: How you travel goes before the verb: 搭地鐵 + 返工.

p: I eat at home in the evening
why: When and where both go before the verb: 夜晚 + 喺屋企 + 食飯.

p: I get up at seven in the morning
why: The time goes before the verb: 朝早七點 + 起身.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 識 (to know how)?
why: 識 is sik1, tone 1; sik6 with tone 6 is 食 (to eat).
識 is for a learned skill and goes right before the verb.
可以 is for permission; 識 is for skills.
唔使 means no need; 唔可以 means not allowed.
會 means will, and the time word stays at the front.

p: I want to work in Hong Kong (start with 我)
why: The place with 喺 goes before the verb: 想 + 喺香港 + 做嘢.
Coffee in a cup takes the classifier 杯: 飲杯咖啡.
唔識 means you never learned how; 唔可以 means you are not allowed.

p: I can speak Cantonese. (I learned it.)
why: 識 is for a learned skill like a language.
鍾意 means like; 好鍾意 is really like.
唔使 means no need; 唔要 means you do not want something.

p: I'd like to buy two books
why: Books take the classifier 本: 兩本書, after 想買.

p: I have to go to work at nine tomorrow
why: The time goes before the verb: 聽日九點 + 要返工.
識 is for a skill you learned; 可以 is for permission.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 凍 (iced, cold)?
why: 凍 is dung3, tone 3: mid and level.
定 is "or" in a question; 或者 is for statements.
都 goes after the person, in front of 係.

q: 'A milk tea and a pineapple bun, please' =
why: 同 joins two things: 奶茶同菠蘿包.
都 comes first, then 唔 and the verb.

p: I like milk tea too (start with 我)
why: 都 goes before the verb, not at the end like English too.

p: We're all going (start with 我哋)
why: With a group, 都 often means all, and it goes before the verb: 我哋都去.
定 offers the choice in a question; 或者 is only for statements.
In a question that offers a choice, "or" is 定.
都 means also and sits right after the person.

p: I'll go tomorrow or the day after.
why: In a statement, "or" is 或者.
都 goes before the verb, not at the end like English too.

p: I'm going to Hong Kong too
why: 都 goes before the verb: 我都去香港.

p: two cups of tea and a cup of coffee
why: Drinks in cups take the classifier 杯, and 同 joins the two things.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 貴 (expensive)?
why: 貴 is gwai3, tone 3; gwai2 with tone 2 is 鬼 (ghost).
Adjectives work like verbs: no 係, and 好 goes in front.
好 before an adjective means very, or is just glue: 好平 = really cheap.
Adjective + 過 + the other person: 佢高過我.
The describer with 嘅 goes right before 衫, and tops take 件.
The describer with 嘅 goes before the noun, and restaurants take the classifier 間.
呢 + classifier + noun: 呢件衫, then 好平 with no 係.
Adjective + 過 + what you compare with: 熱過琴日.
An adjective takes 好 in front, never 係.
過 after the adjective means than: 高過我.
太 means too: 太甜.
呢 + classifier + noun: 呢件衫, then 好平 with no 係.
The describer with 嘅 goes before the noun: 好靚嘅衫, after the classifier 件.
Adjective + 過 + the other person: 佢高過我.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 未 (not yet)?
why: 未 is mei6, tone 6: low and level; 美國 (mei5 gwok3) starts with tone 5.
冇 + verb says it did not happen, and 冇 never takes 咗.
未 before the verb means not yet.
咗 goes right after the verb, and 未 at the end asks "yet?".

q: 'I used to eat dim sum a lot' (a habit) =
why: A past habit takes no 咗: the time word 以前 is enough.
Books take the classifier 本: 買咗兩本書.

p: I went to the doctor yesterday (start with 我)
why: Time goes before the verb: 琴日 + 睇咗醫生.

p: I haven't taken my medicine yet
why: 未 means not yet, and it never takes 咗.
咗 shows the change has happened: 我感冒咗.
冇 + verb is for what did not happen.
…咗…未呀？ asks "have you … yet?".
Time goes before the verb, and books take the classifier 本.
冇 + verb for what did not happen, with the time before the verb: 琴日冇去.
未 means not yet; 冇 means didn't.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 緊 (in the middle of)?
why: 緊 is gan2, tone 2: it rises from the middle.
緊 goes right after the verb, and there is no 係.

q: 'Have you ever been to Hong Kong?' =
why: 過 right after the verb means you have done it at some point.

q: 'She's gone to Central' (and is there now) =
why: 咗 says she went and is there; 過 would only mean she has been there before.
未 before the verb and 過 after it mean never, so far.
Time goes before the verb: 而家 + 食緊飯, with no 係.

p: I went to Macau last week (start with 我)
why: Time goes before the verb: 上個禮拜 + 去咗澳門.

p: Have you ever been to Macau?
why: 過 after the verb asks about experience; 未 at the end makes it a question.
緊 after the verb means you are in the middle of it.

p: Have you ever been to Hong Kong?
why: 過 asks about experience: 去過 = have been.
冇 + verb + 過 means never.
Time goes before the verb: 而家 + 食緊飯, with no 係.

p: I went to Macau last week
why: Time goes before the verb: 上個禮拜 + 去咗澳門.

p: I've never been to Hong Kong
why: 未 or 冇 before the verb and 過 after it mean never.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 嚟 (to come)?
why: 嚟 is lei4, tone 4: low and falling.
How you travel goes first: 搭地鐵 + 去中環.
嚟 + place, and 吖 at the end makes it an invitation.
返 is for going back to a place that is yours, like home.

q: On a minibus, how do you tell the driver you want to get off ahead?
why: 前面有落 is the set phrase: "getting off ahead".

p: I take the MTR to Central (start with 我)
why: How you travel goes before the verb: 搭地鐵 + 去中環.

p: I go to work by bus (start with 我)
why: How you travel goes before the verb: 坐巴士 + 返工.

p: Come over to my place for dinner!
why: 嚟 is come, toward the speaker, and 吖 makes it an invitation.

p: I take the MTR to Central.
why: 去 + place, with no word for "to".
返 is for going back to your own place: 返屋企.
落車 is to get off; 上車 is to get on.

p: I take the MTR to Central
why: How you travel goes before the verb: 搭地鐵 + 去中環.
How you travel goes before the verb: 行路 + 返工.
How you travel goes before the verb: 搭的士 + 返屋企.
喺 is hai2, tone 2; 係 is hai6, tone 6 (to be).
The place word comes after its landmark: 銀行對面.
轉左 is turn left; 轉右 is turn right.
Thing + 喺 + 邊度: the question word stays where the answer goes.

q: In 直行 (go straight), how is 行 read?
why: 行 is haang4 (walk) here; hong4 is its reading in 銀行.

p: I'll wait for you across from the bank (start with 我)
why: The place goes before the verb: 喺銀行對面 + 等你.

p: That bank is across the road
why: 嗰 + classifier + noun: banks take the classifier 間.
A verb-not-verb question asks if it is far: 遠唔遠呀？

p: The MTR station is across from the bank.
why: 對面 is across from; it comes after the landmark 銀行.
喺 (hai2) means at or in; 係 (hai6) means to be.

p: Go straight, and turn right at the traffic lights.
why: 轉右 is turn right.

p: I'll wait for you across from the bank
why: The place goes before the verb: 喺銀行對面 + 等你.

p: That restaurant is next to the bank
why: 嗰 + classifier + noun: restaurants take the classifier 間.

p: Excuse me, where's the MTR station?
why: Thing + 喺 + 邊度, with 喺 (at), not 係.

q: Which is the Jyutping of 吖 (the invitation particle)?
why: 吖 is aa1, tone 1: high; 呀 is aa3, tone 3.
不如 opens the suggestion and 吖 at the end makes it an invitation.

q: A friend invites you, but you can't go. The polite answer is:
why: 下次啦 (next time) is the soft way to say no.
唔好 + verb means don't.
得唔得 asks if a plan is OK, after the time.

p: How about going for dim sum tomorrow? (start with 不如)
why: Time goes before the verb: 聽日 + 去飲茶.

p: Let's eat together! (start with 我哋)
why: 一齊 (together) goes before the verb: 一齊食飯.
唔好 + verb means don't; 冇 is for what did not happen.

p: How about going for dim sum?
why: 吖 (or 啦) at the end makes it a friendly suggestion.
一齊 means together and sits before the verb.
唔好 + verb means don't; 唔使擔心 (no need to worry) also works.

p: How about going for dim sum tomorrow?
why: Time goes before the verb: 不如 + 聽日 + 去飲茶.

p: How about taking a taxi there? (use 不如)
why: How you travel goes before the verb: 搭的士 + 去.
一齊 goes before the verb, and 吖 makes it an invitation.
